commitResults.messageTitle: Add non-functional requirements to developer guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The Non-Functional Requirements section contains the generic AB3
placeholders, which do not reflect TutorRoster's target users or the
project constraints.

Let's replace them with measurable requirements specific to
TutorRoster, grouped by environment and portability, performance,
usability, reliability and data, and privacy and scope.

Behaviour already specified per feature (e.g. error messages,
automatic saving) is left to the functional requirements to avoid
duplication. Performance targets are sized for a single tutor managing
a small group of students and guardians.

Closes #42

commitResults.messageTitle: Define role, contact method, normalised value
commitResults.messageBody:
The feature specification and NFRs rely on these terms, but the
glossary does not define them, so readers may interpret them
differently from what we intend.

Let's add definitions for role, contact method and normalised value
to the glossary.
Add role selection when adding contacts

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject extra text after list command
commitResults.messageBody:
The list command ignores any text typed after it, so input such as
"list 3" is silently accepted.

The MVP spec requires such input to be rejected with
"Invalid list command. Use: list".

Let's add a ListCommandParser that rejects any non-blank arguments,
and route the list command word through it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show contact count in list result
commitResults.messageBody:
The list command always shows "Listed all persons.", which does not
tell the tutor how many contacts there are.

The MVP spec requires "Listed X contacts", or "No contacts found."
when there are no saved contacts.

Let's show the number of contacts in the result, using the singular
"contact" when there is exactly one.

Let's also add a formatContactCount helper in Messages so that the
find command can reuse the same wording.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match find term as partial name
commitResults.messageBody:
The find command splits the input into keywords and matches whole
words only, so "find ale" does not match "Alex Tan".

The MVP spec treats the input as a single search term that matches
any part of a name, ignoring case.

Let's,
* replace NameContainsKeywordsPredicate with
  NameContainsSubstringPredicate
* trim the search term and reduce consecutive spaces to one
* reject a blank term with "Invalid find command. Use: find NAME"
* show "Found X contacts matching: NAME." or
  "No contacts found matching: NAME"

commitResults.messageTitle: Update user guide for list and find
commitResults.messageBody:
The user guide describes the original list and find behaviour: list
ignores extra parameters, and find matches whole keywords with an OR
search.

Both commands now follow the MVP spec, so the guide is inaccurate.

Let's,
* describe list rejecting extra text and showing the contact count
* describe find matching a single, partial, case-insensitive name
* remove the find screenshot, which no longer matches the behaviour
* update the find format in the command summary
Align edit command messages with MVP spec

The contact list is shown in the order contacts were added, which
makes it hard to locate a contact in a long list.

The MVP spec requires contacts to be ordered alphabetically by
normalised name, ignoring capitalisation, wherever the list is shown.

Let's,
* add a PersonDisplayOrderComparator that compares contacts by name,
  ignoring case and treating consecutive spaces as one
* expose a sorted view of the filtered list from ModelManager, so
  indexes used by delete and edit follow the order on screen

commitResults.messageTitle: Order guardians before students with same name
commitResults.messageBody:
Contacts with the same name are ordered only by name, so a guardian
and a student who share a name can appear in either order.

The MVP spec requires contacts with the same name to be ordered by
role, with guardians before students.

Let's compare contacts by role when their names are equal, ranking
guardians before students.

The user guide does not say how contacts are ordered, and the
developer guide describes the model's list as filtered only.

Contacts are now sorted by name and then role, and index numbers
follow this order, so users and developers need to know about it.

Let's,
* add a note on contact order to the user guide
* mention the sorting in the developer guide's Model component
[#81] Update delete command documentation
[#70] Update e/EMAIL to match MVP specifications
[#67] Support e/NONE to remove email in edit

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract contact method formatting into shared helper
commitResults.messageBody:
The UI shows a missing phone number or email address as
"Not provided" in three places: PersonDetailsPanel has its own helper
for phone numbers, and both PersonDetailsPanel and PersonCard repeat
the same Optional-to-text expression for emails.

Keeping one display rule in several places lets the list and the
detail panel drift apart when the rule changes, for example when
phone numbers also become optional.

Let's add a ContactDisplayFormatter with one helper for text values
and one for optional values, and use it in both PersonDetailsPanel
and PersonCard. What the user sees is unchanged.

Let's also move the helper's tests out of LinkUiTest, which only runs
on Windows, so that they run on every platform.

ContactDisplayFormatter only has static methods, but its implicit
public constructor still allows instances to be created. Coverage
tools also count this constructor as an untested line.

Let's add a private constructor so that the class cannot be
instantiated.
Select edited contact after edit

commitResults.messageTitle: Show role beside name on list cards
commitResults.messageBody:
Each list card shows the contact's role on its own line, below the
name.

The MVP spec shows each contact in the list as "NAME [ROLE]", for
example "Alex Tan [Student]", so that contacts with the same name
can be told apart at a glance.

Let's,
* add a formatNameWithRole helper to ContactDisplayFormatter
* show the name and role together on the card's first line
* remove the separate role line from the card

commitResults.messageTitle: Label phone and email on list cards
commitResults.messageBody:
Each list card shows the contact's phone number and email address
without labels, so the two lines are hard to tell apart, and a
missing value is shown only as "Not provided".

The MVP spec shows each contact in the list with "Phone: " and
"Email: " labels, and "Not provided" for a missing value.

Let's prefix the phone and email lines with their labels, and format
both values with ContactDisplayFormatter so that a missing value is
shown as "Not provided", as in the detail panel.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe list card format in user guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The user guide does not say what each contact in the list shows, so
users cannot tell what to expect from list and find.

Let's describe the format of each list entry, including the role
beside the name, the phone and email labels, and "Not provided" for
a missing phone number or email address.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove unused text overload of formatContactMethod
commitResults.messageBody:
ContactDisplayFormatter has two formatContactMethod methods: one for
text values and one for optional values. Since phone numbers became
optional, the UI formats both phone numbers and email addresses as
optional values, so the text overload is no longer used.

Unused code has to be read and maintained without benefit.

Let's remove the text overload and its tests, and add a test for a
present phone number so that both kinds of contact method stay
covered.
[#99]  Add command must have either phone or name field

commitResults.messageTitle: Show linked guardian on student list cards
commitResults.messageBody:
Student list cards do not show the student's guardian, so the tutor
has to select each student to see who their guardian is.

The MVP spec requires the list to show linked guardian details for
each student, as "Guardian: NAME", or "Guardian: None" if the student
has no linked guardian.

Let's,
* pass the full contact list to PersonListPanel, so that a guardian
  hidden by find can still be shown on the student's card
* show "Guardian: NAME" or "Guardian: None" on student cards only
* add a formatGuardianName helper to ContactDisplayFormatter

commitResults.messageTitle: Refresh student cards when guardian changes
commitResults.messageBody:
A student's list card shows the name of its linked guardian, but the
card is only redrawn when the student's own record changes.

After a guardian is renamed with edit, the cards of the guardian's
students keep showing the old name until the list is refreshed.

Let's redraw the list cards whenever any contact changes, so that
each student's card shows the current name of its guardian.

commitResults.messageTitle: Wrap long names on list cards
commitResults.messageBody:
A list card shows the contact's name and role on a single line. Names
may have up to 70 characters, so a long name followed by its role can
be cut off at small window sizes, or widen the list beyond the
window.

The GUI should remain usable at a resolution of 1280x720 and a screen
scale of 150%.

Let's let the name label wrap onto further lines, and make each list
cell fit the width of the list so that wrapping takes effect.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe guardian line on list cards in user guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The user guide's description of each list entry does not mention the
linked guardian, which student cards now show.

Let's add the guardian line to the example list entry, and state that
"Guardian: None" is shown for a student without a linked guardian.

PersonDisplayOrderComparatorTest checks that a guardian is ordered
before a student with the same name, but no test checks this order in
the list that ModelManager exposes to the UI. Such a test was not
possible while contacts with the same name were treated as duplicates.

Contacts with the same name but a different role or contact details
are now allowed, so the order can be checked end to end.

Let's add a ModelManagerTest case that adds a student and then a
guardian with the same name, and checks that the guardian is
displayed first.

StringUtil#containsWordIgnoreCase was used only by the original find
command, which matched whole words. The find command now matches any
part of a name, so the method is no longer used outside its own
tests.

Unused code has to be read and maintained without benefit.

Let's remove the method, its tests, and the imports that only it
used.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe list and find in developer guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The developer guide's Implementation section covers linking, Add
validation and saving, but not how list and find work.

Developers changing these commands need to know how input is
validated, how names are matched and what results are reported.

Let's add a section describing ListCommandParser and ListCommand,
and how FindCommandParser normalises the search term and
NameContainsSubstringPredicate matches it against names.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find sequence diagram to developer guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The developer guide describes find in prose only, which makes the
order of interactions between the parser, the command and the model
hard to follow.

Let's add a sequence diagram for "find ale", in the same style as the
existing delete sequence diagram, showing how the predicate is
created and applied to the model's filtered list.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe contact ordering and list cards in guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The developer guide mentions that the model's list is sorted, but not
how contacts are ordered, why sorting happens in the model, or how
the list cards show contact details and linked guardians.

Developers need this to keep displayed indexes consistent and to
change the list cards safely.

Let's describe PersonDisplayOrderComparator and the sorted view in
ModelManager, how PersonCard and PersonListPanel display contacts
and guardians, and the design alternatives considered for sorting
and for matching names in find.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add manual tests for find to developer guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The manual testing appendix has steps for adding, deleting and editing
contacts, but none for find. Testers have to work out the expected
results and messages from the code or the user guide.

Let's add find test cases that create their own contacts, since the app
no longer starts with sample data.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add manual tests for list to developer guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The manual testing appendix covers find, but not list. Testers cannot
easily check the empty list message, the singular and plural contact
counts, or the error for extra text after list.

Let's add list test cases that start from an empty address book and
add contacts one at a time.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add manual tests for contact order and list cards
commitResults.messageBody:
The manual testing appendix does not cover how contacts are ordered or
what each list card shows. Testers cannot easily check that guardians
come before students with the same name, or that a student's card
updates when its guardian is renamed.

Let's add test cases for the display order, the card details, the
guardian line and the wrapping of long names.

commitResults.messageTitle: Wrap contact details on list cards
commitResults.messageBody:
Only the name on a list card wraps onto further lines. Email addresses
have no length limit and guardian names may have up to 70 characters,
so a long email or guardian line is cut off with an ellipsis. The
specification requires list to show each contact's complete details.

Let's let the phone, email and guardian labels wrap as well.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe wrapping of list card details in guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The developer guide describes what each list card shows, but not that
long details wrap. Readers may assume a long email or guardian name
is cut off, as it was before.

Let's state that every line on the card wraps, so details are shown
in full.

commitResults.messageTitle: Sort accented names with their unaccented forms
commitResults.messageBody:
Contacts are sorted by comparing lower-case names character by
character. Names may contain any Unicode letter, and accented letters
have larger character codes than all unaccented letters, so
"Élise Tan" is displayed after "Zoe Lim".

Users expect such names to appear with the unaccented letter, and
indexes would otherwise be harder to find in a long list.

Let's compare names with their accents removed first, by decomposing
them with Normalizer and removing the combining marks. Names that are
still equal are compared with their accents, so names that differ only
in accents have a fixed order.

Collator is not used because it ignores spaces and some punctuation,
which would place "Alexa Lim" before "Alex Tan".

The User Guide and Developer Guide do not say how names with accented
letters are ordered.

Let's describe the new ordering and why Normalizer is used instead of
Collator.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use contact wording in user-facing messages
commitResults.messageBody:
Several messages shown to users are inherited from AddressBook-Level3.
They refer to a "person" or an "address book", while the rest of
TutorRoster refers to contacts. The help window also links to the
AddressBook-Level3 user guide.

Mixed terminology makes the app feel inconsistent and can be reported
as a bug during peer testing.

Let's,
* use "contact" and "TutorRoster" in the add, edit, clear and exit
  messages, and in the data file error messages
* report a successful add as "Added contact: NAME [ROLE].", matching
  the delete and edit messages
* link the help window to the TutorRoster user guide
* remove Messages#format and MESSAGE_INVALID_PERSON_DISPLAYED_INDEX,
  which are no longer used

Class and variable names such as Person are left unchanged, as they
are not visible to users and renaming them would affect most files.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update User Guide to use contact wording
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide still describes the add, edit, list and clear commands
using "person" and "address book", which do not match the wording used
by the app.

Let's update these headings, descriptions and examples to refer to
contacts and TutorRoster.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace AddressBook wording on home page and DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The project website's home page still describes AddressBook-Level3,
with its title, CI badges and links. The Developer Guide is titled
"AB-3 Developer Guide", and its manual testing instructions refer to
persons and an address book.

These pages are read by users and evaluators, so the leftover
template text makes the product look unfinished.

Let's,
* describe TutorRoster on the home page, using the badges and
  acknowledgement from the README
* rename the Developer Guide and use contact wording in its manual
  testing instructions

commitResults.messageTitle: Show and select new contact after add
commitResults.messageBody:
After a find, the displayed list stays filtered when a contact is
added. If the new contact does not match the search term, it is saved
but not shown. The add result also carries no contact ID, so the new
contact is never selected and the detail panel does not show it.

Users may think the add failed, and the behavior differs from edit and
link, which select the contact they change.

Let's,
* reset the filter after a successful add so that all contacts are
  shown
* return the new contact's ID so that the UI selects it

A failed add keeps the existing filter, as LogicManager discards the
candidate model when a command fails.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document list refresh and selection after add
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide and Developer Guide do not say what the contact list
shows after a contact is added.

Let's describe that all contacts are shown and the new contact is
selected, and how AddCommand achieves this.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test full display of long details in narrow list
commitResults.messageBody:
The existing test only checks that the detail labels on a list card
have text wrapping enabled. It does not show that long values are
displayed in full when the contact list is narrow.

The Developer Guide states that long names, email addresses and
guardian names are shown in full, so this should be verified with the
actual list layout.

Let's add a test that shows a contact with a long name, phone number,
email address and guardian name in a list at its minimum width, and
checks that
* each detail is displayed without being cut off
* each detail stays within the card
* the card is taller than a card with short details
* no horizontal scroll bar is shown

commitResults.messageTitle: Treat curly apostrophes as straight in find
commitResults.messageBody:
Names may contain a straight apostrophe (') or a curly one, which is
common in text copied from messaging apps. Find compares the
characters exactly, so "find o'brien" does not match "O’Brien". The
list order also places "O’Brien" after "Zoe", as the curly apostrophe
has a larger character code than all letters.

Tutors usually type the straight apostrophe, so contacts copied from
messaging apps are hard to find and to locate in the list.

Let's add Name#replaceCurlyApostrophes and use it when
* matching names and search terms in find
* ordering names in the contact list

Stored names are left unchanged, so they are displayed as entered.

The User Guide and Developer Guide do not say how find handles curly
and straight apostrophes.

Let's describe that they are treated as the same when matching and
ordering names.

commitResults.messageTitle: Order letters such as ø and ł with base letters
commitResults.messageBody:
Accents are removed before names are compared by decomposing each
letter into a base letter and combining marks. Some letters, such as
ø, ł, æ and ß, are separate letters in Unicode and cannot be
decomposed, so "Søren" is still displayed after "Zoe".

Such names would then be hard to locate in the list, which is the
problem this issue fixes for other accented letters.

Let's move the accent removal into Name#removeAccents, and replace
these letters with their base letters from a fixed table after the
combining marks are removed.

A fixed table is used because the Java standard library has no
mapping for these letters, and only a few are used in names.

commitResults.messageTitle: Ignore accents when matching names in find
commitResults.messageBody:
Find compares letters exactly after ignoring case, so "find elise"
does not match "Élise", and "find soren" does not match "Søren". The
contact list already orders these letters with their base letters.

Tutors may not know how to type such letters, so these contacts are
hard to find, and find is inconsistent with the list order.

Let's apply Name#removeAccents, which the list order uses, to both
the name and the search term in find.

Both sides are processed in the same way, so a name that matched
before still matches. Stored names are left unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use American spelling in method names
commitResults.messageBody:
A few method names use British spelling, such as toNormalisedName and
parseCommand_unrecognisedInput_throwsParseException, while others use
American spelling, such as normalizePhone and normalizedName.

The coding standard asks for American spelling, and mixed spelling
makes names harder to search for.

Let's rename these methods to use American spelling.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document ordering of letters such as ø and ł
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide and Developer Guide only describe how letters with
accents are ordered.

Let's describe that letters which cannot be decomposed, such as ø and
ł, are ordered with their base letters, and how this is done.

The User Guide and Developer Guide do not say how find handles
accented letters.

Let's describe that accents are ignored when matching names.

The README, User Guide and Developer Guide use British spelling in a
few places, such as "capitalisation" and "organised", while most of
the documentation uses American spelling, such as "capitalization".

Let's use American spelling throughout for consistency with the code.

MainApp.VERSION is "V0.5.1", inherited from AddressBook-Level3. It is
written to the log when the app starts.

The release steps in the Developer Guide require the version number
to be updated before each release, and v1.3 is about to be released.

Let's set the version to "V1.3".
Add student status to contacts and data file

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix window size for small screens
commitResults.messageBody:
The window opens at 740x600 and cannot be made shorter than 600. The
result display is fixed at 100px.

At 1280x720 with 150% scaling, the screen is about 480 units tall, so
the bottom of the window is cut off. The GUI should be usable at this
resolution and scale.

Let's,
* lower the default window height to 430
* lower the minimum window height to 400
* allow the result display to shrink to 60px when the window is short

The width is kept, as 740 by default and 600 at minimum already fit
the screen.

commitResults.messageTitle: Enable assertions when running the app
commitResults.messageBody:
Assertions are enabled by default for the Gradle test task, but not
for the run task. Assertions that guard internal assumptions are
therefore skipped when the app is launched with ./gradlew run, so
violations go unnoticed during manual testing.

Let's enable assertions for the run task too, so that both automated
and manual testing check the same assumptions.
[#151] Bug fix for adding a contact
Add archive and unarchive commands for students
Hide former students from list and add list former

commitResults.messageTitle: Add view command to show a contact's details
commitResults.messageBody:
The details panel shows a contact only after a mouse click, or as a
side effect of edit or link. Tutors who prefer typing cannot open a
contact's full record directly from the command box.

Let's add view INDEX, which selects the contact at INDEX in the
displayed list so that the details panel shows it. The displayed list
and the saved data are left unchanged.

The two index error messages are added to Messages rather than copied
into ViewCommand, as a step towards removing the copies in other
commands (#163).

commitResults.messageTitle: Document view command in user guide
commitResults.messageBody:
Add a section for view INDEX after find, and a row in the command
summary.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace list former flag with a contact filter
commitResults.messageBody:
ListCommand stores a boolean that chooses between showing active
contacts and former students. Each new list filter, such as role,
level or subject, would need another boolean and another branch.

Let's introduce ContactFilter, a predicate holding an optional role and
a student status, and pass it to ListCommand instead of the boolean.
The predicates in Model now refer to the same filters, so the rules
for active and former contacts live in one place.

This commit does not change what list shows. Filtering by role is
added in the next commit.

list shows guardians and active students together. Tutors who want to
see only their students, or only the guardians to contact, have to
scan the whole list.

Let's accept an optional r/ROLE in list, so that list r/student and
list r/guardian show only contacts with that role. r/ can be combined
with st/former, so list r/student st/former shows former students.

Guardians are never former, so list r/guardian st/former is rejected
with a clear message instead of showing an empty list. Unknown
parameters, repeated parameters and invalid roles are also rejected,
following the list filter spec (#157).

commitResults.messageTitle: Document role filter for list in user guide
commitResults.messageBody:
Add the r/ROLE parameter to the list section, with a table of common
list commands, and update the command summary.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain empty results when listing by role
commitResults.messageBody:
list r/student and list r/guardian show "No contacts found." when no
contact matches. If every student is former, list r/student gives no
hint that former students exist, unlike plain list.

Let's name the role in the message, and suggest list r/student
st/former when the only students are former ones.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain unknown parameter pattern in list parser
commitResults.messageBody:
The regular expression for unknown parameters is hard to read at a
glance. Let's add a comment with examples of what it matches.

commitResults.messageTitle: Mention former students in view section of user guide
commitResults.messageBody:
view works on the results of list st/former and find, where former
students appear. Let's say so, and show how a former student's role
is displayed in the details panel.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fit restored window to the screen
commitResults.messageBody:
The window is restored to the size and position saved in
preferences.json. A saved window can be taller than the screen, or lie
outside every screen after a monitor is disconnected, so part of the
window is cut off. Lowering the default height does not help in these
cases, and makes the window too short to show more than one contact on
normal screens.

Let's,
* shrink and move the restored window so that it fits on the screen it
  is on, or on the primary screen if it is on none
* restore the default height of 600

Saved sizes and positions that already fit are kept as they are.

The fitting is done in GuiSettings, so that it can be unit tested
without a screen.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove fixed off-screen window known issue
commitResults.messageBody:
The user guide lists a known issue where the window opens off-screen
after switching from multiple screens to one.

The window is now moved onto a screen when it is restored, so the issue
no longer occurs.

Let's remove it from the list of known issues.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for restoring the window position
commitResults.messageBody:
MainWindow fits the restored window to the screen it is on. No test
restores a window that has a saved position, so finding the screen of
the saved window is not tested.

Let's add UI tests that restore one window saved on the screen and one
saved off the screen.

Like LinkUiTest, they run only on Windows, as they need a desktop
JavaFX runtime.
[144] Add optional level and subject for students

commitResults.messageTitle: Link docs to the team repository instead of AB3
commitResults.messageBody:
The developer guide and the DevOps page link Main, MainApp, Ui,
MainWindow, Logic, Model and Storage to the AB3 repository. Those
files differ from ours, so the links show code that TutorRoster no
longer has.

Let's point the links to the same files in our repository. The
acknowledgement on the home page still links to AB3, as it credits the
original project.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document list filtering in developer guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The developer guide still describes list as rejecting any text and
resetting the filter to PREDICATE_SHOW_ALL_PERSONS. Since list r/ROLE
and list st/former, neither is true.

Let's describe how ListCommandParser builds a ContactFilter and how
ListCommand applies it, add a sequence diagram for list r/student, and
record the design choices behind the filter: using list rather than
find, a separate st/ prefix, and one filter object instead of flags.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update manual tests for listing and filtering contacts
commitResults.messageBody:
The manual test for invalid list input expects the old usage message,
and there are no manual tests for filtering by role.

Let's update the expected message and add test cases for list r/ROLE,
its combination with st/former, and its error messages.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify list parser details in developer guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The list filtering section says the parser rejects any word ending in
"/", which does not cover a prefix such as n/ in n/Alex. It also omits
that st/ values other than former are rejected, links the error order
to add without saying how, and mentions an isFormerList flag that new
developers have never seen.

Let's describe the rejected prefixes with an example, add the rule for
other st/ values, state that list checks values in a fixed order like
add, and drop the reference to the old flag.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add class and activity diagrams for list filtering
commitResults.messageBody:
The list filtering section explains ContactFilter and the parser checks
in text only, with a numbered list of five checks. The classes involved
and the order of the checks are easier to follow as diagrams.

Let's add a class diagram of ContactFilter and the classes that use it,
and an activity diagram of the checks ListCommandParser makes. The
numbered list is replaced by short notes on each kind of error, so the
diagram and the text do not repeat each other.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe planned list filters in developer guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The developer guide does not say how list will support st/all, level
or subject, although ContactFilter was designed for them.

Let's add a proposed section explaining how each would extend
ContactFilter, so future developers know where these filters belong.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move list design considerations into listing section
commitResults.messageBody:
The design considerations for list filtering sit under "Ordering and
displaying contacts", away from the listing section they explain. The
proposed filters also mention st/active without saying what it does.

Let's move the three list aspects to a design considerations heading
at the end of "Listing and finding contacts", explain st/active, and
reflow one bullet whose lines were wrapped unevenly.

commitResults.messageTitle: Address review comments on list filtering DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The activity diagram combines unknown prefixes and repeated prefixes
into one format error, although the parser gives each its own message,
and it does not show that text before the first prefix is rejected.
The sequence diagram creates ContactFilter with a bare role, while the
constructor takes an Optional. The manual tests do not cover status
validation.

Let's give repeated prefixes their own branch, name extra text in the
first condition, show Optional.of(STUDENT) in the sequence diagram,
and add manual tests for a repeated st/ and for st/active.

commitResults.messageTitle: Filter list by any student status
commitResults.messageBody:
list accepts only st/former. Tutors cannot list all students, active
and former, in one view, and typing list former or list st/all gives a
general format error with no hint of what was meant. Plain list also
hides former students without saying so.

Let's accept st/active, st/former and st/all, with all represented as
an empty status in ContactFilter so that it matches any status. Invalid
or empty st/ values now get their own message. When a list hides
former students that would otherwise match, the success message says
how many and suggests st/all. A single role or status word without its
prefix, such as list former, gets a "Did you mean" suggestion.

The rules follow the list filter spec in #157.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document status filters for list in user guide
commitResults.messageBody:
Describe st/active, st/former and st/all, the new status error, the

former student, and update the command summary.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update developer guide for status filters
commitResults.messageBody:
The developer guide describes st/ as accepting only former, shows the
status in ContactFilter as required, and lists st/active and st/all as
proposed.

Let's describe the optional status and ALL_CONTACTS, the status error,
the suggestion for a missing prefix and the note on hidden former
students. Update both diagrams for the optional status, keep only level
and subject in the proposed section, and update the manual tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Restyle contact list, command box and results
commitResults.messageBody:
The main window uses the AddressBook dark theme. A contact's role and
status are shown as text in square brackets after the name, and a
failed command looks the same as a successful one in the result
display. The theme also asks for Segoe UI, which exists only on
Windows.

This makes it hard to tell students, guardians and former students
apart at a glance, and easy to miss that a command has failed.

Let's,
* show the role and the former status as colored badges after the
  name
* show successful results in green and errors in red
* add a ">" prompt and a monospace font to the command box
* use the system font and one dark blue-gray palette
* make the contact cards shorter

Command messages, and the phone, email, guardian, level and subject
lines on each card, stay the same.

The tests that looked for "NAME [ROLE]" on a card now check the name
and the badges instead.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test long former student name in narrow list
commitResults.messageBody:
A former student's card shows the name, the role badge and the former
badge on one line. In the narrowest contact list, a long name has to
wrap to leave room for both badges. No test checks this.

Let's add a test that shows a former student with a long name in the
narrowest list, and checks that the name and both badges are shown in
full within the card.

Suggested in the review of #207.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test archive and unarchive in all-status list
commitResults.messageBody:
Status commands keep the current filter, but no test covered the
list st/all view added for #162. Existing tests only cover the default
list, the former-only list and search results.

Let's run list st/all, then archive and unarchive a linked student
through LogicManager, and check that the student stays shown with the
same ID and guardian link after each change.

The details panel lists the role, phone, email, level, subject and
guardian details as one column of lines. The guardian's details blend
into the student's, and the panel does not match the contact list,
which shows the role as a badge.

Let's,
* show the role and former badges next to the name, as on the cards
* group the lines into Details, Tuition and Guardian sections
* hide the sections when no contact is selected
* hide the empty guardian phone and email lines when there is no
  guardian
* log which contact is shown, by its ID only, so that no personal
  details are written to the log file

Each line keeps its text, so the tests that check the panel's text
stay the same.

The badge code moves from PersonCard into RoleBadges, so that the
cards and the panel share it. The panel shows a different contact on
each selection, so RoleBadges also replaces the previous role style.

commitResults.messageTitle: Share one helper to show or hide UI nodes
commitResults.messageBody:
RoleBadges, PersonCard and PersonDetailsPanel each set a node's
visible and managed flags by hand. The details panel and RoleBadges
also assert role rules that Person's constructor already checks.

Repeating the two flags makes it easy to hide a node but leave its
space behind. The asserts can never fail for a valid Person, and
Codecov counts each one as a partly covered line.

Let's,
* add UiUtil#setShown and use it in all three classes
* remove the two asserts, as Person already enforces both rules

This keeps the "hide and free its space" rule in one place.

commitResults.messageTitle: Round corners of details panel section border
commitResults.messageBody:
Each details panel section has a rounded background, but its left
border keeps square corners.

The amber border of the Guardian section sticks out past the rounded
background, so the corners look uneven.

Let's give the section border the same radius as its background, as
the command box does.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe details panel sections in user guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The view section of the user guide describes the details panel as a
plain list of lines. It does not mention the badges, the Tuition
section or that view works after list st/all.

Users may not recognise the new panel from this description.

Let's,
* describe the badges beside the name
* list the Details, Tuition and Guardian sections
* mention list st/all among the lists view works on

The screenshots are updated separately in #167.

commitResults.messageTitle: Filter list by level and subject
commitResults.messageBody:
The list command filters by role and status only. A tutor preparing
for a lesson also needs to see, for example, only Sec 3 students or
only students taking A-Math.

Let's,
* add lv/LEVEL and sub/SUBJECT to list, as optional Level and Subject
  fields in ContactFilter
* match values with Level#isSameValue and Subject#isSameValue, so
  letter case and spaces are ignored, as in add and edit
* parse values with ParserUtil, so their errors match add and edit
* reject r/guardian with lv/ or sub/, as guardians have no level or
  subject, in the same way as r/guardian st/former
* show "No contacts found." when a level or subject filter matches
  nothing, followed by the hidden-former-students note if any
* log the filter and counts at FINE level in ListCommand

Matching whole values keeps sub/Math from also showing A-Math students.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document level and subject filters in user guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The user guide describes list with r/ROLE and st/STATUS only.

Let's add lv/LEVEL and sub/SUBJECT to the list format, examples,
matching rules, error messages and command summary.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update developer guide for level and subject filters
commitResults.messageBody:
The developer guide lists level and subject filters as proposed, and
its list diagrams show role and status only.

Let's,
* describe the Level and Subject fields of ContactFilter and how they
  match
* add the new checks to the parser activity diagram and the class
  diagram, and the new constructor arguments to the sequence diagram
* add manual tests for lv/ and sub/
* remove the proposed section

ContactFilter has getLevel() and getSubject(), but nothing calls them.
ListCommand only needs to know whether a level or subject is chosen,
which hasStudentDetail() already answers.

Let's remove both getters to keep the class to what is used. They can
be added back if a caller needs them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Note that ContactFilter equality is exact
commitResults.messageBody:
ContactFilter matches levels and subjects ignoring letter case and
spaces, but equals compares them exactly. Filters for "sec3" and
"Sec 3" therefore match the same contacts without being equal, which
can surprise a reader of ListCommand#equals or its tests.

Let's document this in the Javadoc of ContactFilter#equals. Exact
equality is kept, as it only affects command equality in tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report no contacts for empty former level filter
commitResults.messageBody:
list st/former lv/Sec 4 with no matches shows "No former students
found.", even when there are former students at other levels. The
message suggests there are no former students at all.

Let's check for an empty level or subject result before the
former-only status, so such a filter shows "No contacts found.", as
the developer guide describes for level and subject filters.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move shared index messages into Messages
commitResults.messageBody:
DeleteCommand, EditCommand and StudentStatusCommand each define their
own copy of the invalid-index and contact-not-found messages, although
Messages already has both for ViewCommand. If one copy is reworded,
the commands show different errors for the same mistake.

Let's remove the copies and use Messages.MESSAGE_INVALID_CONTACT_INDEX
and Messages.MESSAGE_CONTACT_NOT_FOUND in these commands, their parsers
and their tests. The messages shown to users do not change.

LinkCommand keeps its own messages, as they name the student or
guardian index.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test undo in a level and subject view
commitResults.messageBody:
Undo restores the filter that was shown when a contact was deleted.
No test checks that this filter keeps its level and subject, so
undo could show contacts outside the original view without a test
failing.

Let's add a test that lists Sec 3 Math students, deletes one, switches
to list st/all and then undoes. It checks that the level and subject
filter is back, that only matching students are shown, and that the
restored student is selected.
163 Move shared index messages into Messages

commitResults.messageTitle: Add hashCode and null check to find classes
commitResults.messageBody:
NameContainsSubstringPredicate overrides equals but not hashCode, so
two equal predicates can have different hash codes. This breaks the
contract of Object#hashCode, and would misbehave if a predicate were
ever stored in a hash-based collection. FindCommand also accepts a
null predicate, which only fails later when the command runs, and its
public constructor has no Javadoc.

Let's add a hashCode based on the search term, and check the
FindCommand predicate for null in a documented constructor, with a
test for each.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rank roles with a switch in the display order
commitResults.messageBody:
PersonDisplayOrderComparator ranks a guardian first and every other
role second. If a role is added, it is ranked as a student without
any warning, and the order may be wrong.

Let's rank roles with a switch expression over Role, so that adding a
role without giving it a rank fails to compile.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add boundary and EP cases to view and find tests
commitResults.messageBody:
The view tests check the first index and the first index past the
list, but not the last valid index or the largest index that can be
parsed. The find tests check matching names, but not how long a
search term can be before it stops matching. Most cases also do not
say which partition or boundary they cover.

Let's,
* add the last displayed index, Integer.MAX_VALUE, one past it and a
  plus sign to the view tests
* add single-letter, whole-name and one-character-too-long search
  terms to the find tests
* check that equal find predicates have equal hash codes
* mark the cases with EP or Boundary comments

commitResults.messageTitle: Test every pair of list filter values
commitResults.messageBody:
list takes four optional parameters with 3, 4, 2 and 2 values each,
48 combinations in all. The existing tests pick combinations one
feature at a time, so some pairs of values, such as st/former with
sub/, are never parsed together.

Let's add 11 cases that cover every valid pair of values at least
once, following the all-pairs heuristic, and mark the test with a
Heuristic comment explaining the choice.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add details panel and badges to UI class diagram
commitResults.messageBody:
The UI class diagram and its description show the UI as it was before
the details panel and role badges were added. A reader cannot tell
where a contact's details or its role badges come from.

Let's add PersonDetailsPanel as a part of MainWindow that depends on
the Model, and RoleBadges as a helper used by both PersonCard and
PersonDetailsPanel. The description names the details panel and
explains why both use RoleBadges.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document quoted subjects for list filters
commitResults.messageBody:
list accepts a quoted sub/ value, so a subject such as "Art n/Design"
can be filtered without n/ being rejected as an unknown parameter. The
UG list section and the DG list parser checks do not mention this, so
users only learn it from the add section.

Let's add a quoted example to the UG list section, explain in the DG
that text inside a quoted subject is not checked as a prefix, and add
a manual test that compares the quoted and unquoted forms.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep vowel signs when removing accents
commitResults.messageBody:
Name#removeAccents removes every combining mark. In Latin, Greek and
Cyrillic these are accents, but in scripts such as Devanagari they
include vowel signs that change a name. find किरण therefore also
matches करण, and a term made only of a vowel sign becomes empty and
matches every contact.

Let's remove combining marks only when they follow a Latin, Greek or
Cyrillic letter, and keep them in other scripts. The method now also
reads the text by code point instead of by char.

Accent-insensitive search and ordering for names such as Élise and
Søren do not change. The UG and DG now say that vowel signs in
scripts such as Devanagari must match.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test every kind of combining mark in removeAccents
commitResults.messageBody:
The removeAccents tests use only non-spacing marks after Latin letters
and a spacing vowel sign after a Devanagari letter. Enclosing marks,
non-spacing marks in Devanagari and characters outside the Basic
Multilingual Plane are untested, so a mistake in those paths would
go unnoticed.

Let's add one case for each kind of mark after a Latin and a
Devanagari letter, and for a supplementary character with and without
a mark after it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix contact targeting for same-name students
commitResults.messageBody:
Students with equal names and no contact methods can both be added.
Field equality then selects the first record for an update or removal,
even when the command targets the second displayed student. Linking
can consequently lose one ID and save the other ID twice.

Locate update and removal targets by their immutable contact IDs.
